#2056. Lazio-Roma, biglietti del derby: vendita libera dalle 11 del 24 novembre

Si apre la terza fase per la gara del 13 dicembre; nella vendita libera una persona può acquistare fino a quattro tagliandi.

La vendita libera dei biglietti per Lazio-Roma inizierà martedì 24 novembre alle 11:00. Secondo quanto riportato da Sslazio, Si tratta della terza fase di vendita per il derby, in programma domenica 13 dicembre alle 12:30, come comunicato dalla S.S. Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Dalle 11:00 del 24 novembre la vendita sarà aperta per tutto lo stadio. Per i posti dell’intera Tribuna Tevere resterà però obbligatorio possedere una fidelity card Eagle Card o Millenovecento. Per procedere online occorrerà inserire il codice della card come coupon; il codice potrà anche essere presentato al momento dell’acquisto.

Ai biglietti acquistati online sarà applicata una commissione di servizio del 3,80%. I possessori di una fidelity card Millenovecento o Eagle che non sono abbonati potranno chiedere, anche acquistando online, che il titolo d’ingresso sia caricato elettronicamente sulla card.

I biglietti ridotti per invalidi civili al 100% e quelli di Tribuna Tevere per persone non deambulanti, in entrambi i casi con accompagnatore, potranno essere acquistati soltanto nei Lazio Style 1900, escluso il punto vendita di Parco Leonardo. Il ridotto Under 16 è riservato ai ragazzi nati dal 1° gennaio 2010.

Chi compra fisicamente un biglietto in un punto vendita deve mostrare un documento d’identità: senza, il titolo di accesso non può essere emesso, secondo il D.L. 8/2/2010 n. 8. Non sono considerate idonee alla vendita le patenti di ultima generazione che non riportano il luogo di residenza.

Nella vendita libera ogni persona può acquistare al massimo quattro biglietti, secondo le disposizioni dell’Osservatorio sulle Manifestazioni Sportive. Per gli altri tre eventuali intestatari è sufficiente presentare anche una copia del documento d’identità. I bambini di quattro anni nati dal 1° gennaio 2022 entrano gratuitamente e senza biglietto, mostrando un documento d’identità o la tessera sanitaria. All’ingresso l’identità sarà controllata per ogni spettatore: il documento è obbligatorio anche per i minorenni.

#2055. Conceiçao torna a Parma: il gol da ex con la Lazio e l’esultanza contenuta

L’ex biancoceleste ricorda l’unica stagione in gialloblù e parla dell’emozione di essere di nuovo in città dopo 26 anni.

Sergio Conceiçao è tornato a Parma per la sfida contro la Roma. In un’intervista a Gianluca Di Marzio ha ricordato il periodo trascorso in gialloblù, dopo l’esperienza alla Lazio, e un gol segnato al Parma da ex con la maglia biancoceleste, dopo il quale esultò poco.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Parma è stata la seconda squadra italiana di Conceiçao, dopo la Lazio. Il suo ritorno gli ha fatto ripensare all’anno trascorso in città: «È un’emozione, un piacere grandissimo tornare qua. Ho vissuto una stagione importante. Sono rimasto solo un anno, ma è stato veramente bello. Mi fa molto piacere ricordare i bei momenti passati qui».

Tra i ricordi dell’ex biancoceleste c’è anche la rete realizzata contro il Parma. Conceiçao ha raccontato di aver contenuto l’esultanza: «Dopo il gol col Parma da ex, alla Lazio, non ho esultato tanto, ma resta un ricordo bellissimo».

Antonio Cassano, dagli studi di "Viva El Futbol", ha analizzato il pareggio ottenuto dall'Inter sul campo dell'Atalanta: "Il peggior nemico dell'Inter è l'Inter. Decide l'Inter se giocar bene, se giocar male, prende il Como e lo distrugge. L'Inter decide le sorti del campionato: è più forte, più coraggiosa, ha più qualità, più lunghezza della rosa. Sono convinto che l'Inter ha una grandissima distanza sulla Roma, è la più forte in assoluto".

"Spence? Per me è una pippa, faceva panchina al Genoa, al Tottenham giocava e non giocava, poi si è ritrovato a giocare al Mondiale. Non mi piaceva tanto Dumfries, ma era funzionale a tutta fascia, tutta la vita lui. Tutta la vita anche Diouf, che non sto capendo cosa sta succedendo, prima giocava, era titolare fisso, convocato anche da Zidane. Adesso, tutto d'un tratto, gioca sempre Spence, che è un giocatore improponibile, ha rimesso lui in gioco l'Atalanta, regala il calcio d'angolo perchè ha la palla sul destro per rinviare o eventualmente proteggere, la proteggi sempre dalla parte del fallo laterale. Se tu fai una giocata al contrario, il calcio nella tua testa non c'entra niente: puoi giocare a basket, a baseball, tutt'altro. Uno che gioca nell'Inter e nell'Inghilterra non può fare un errore del genere".

"L'Inter era in gestione: 3-1, 4-2. La qualità dell'Inter anche quando entra Jones, che è il centrocampista più forte dopo Calhanoglu perchè Mkhitaryan ormai è in fase calante ma ha fatto una buona partita. Stankovic è un giovane, non posso pensare che entri 15 minuti e non corre. Non hai tolto Xavi, Iniesta e Messi. I cambi di Chivu? Ma se non metti Lautaro sul 4-2 quando lo metti? La gente critica Lautaro per cosa? Un mese e mezzo che sta fermo, l'hai buttato dentro sul 4-2 per farlo giocare un pochino. Non vai a pensare al disastro che l'Inter ha fatto, buttando via 2 punti".

#2053. Digard pronto alla sua prima Champions: "Mi sento come un bambino a Disneyland"

Didier Digard non nasconde l’entusiasmo alla vigilia della sua prima esperienza in Champions League. Il nuovo allenatore del Lens guiderà infatti la squadra nella trasferta contro il Lipsia, valida per la quinta giornata della fase campionato, vivendo un momento speciale della sua carriera.

Intervenuto in conferenza stampa prima della sfida alla Red Bull Arena, il tecnico francese ha raccontato con grande sincerità le proprie sensazioni. Digard ha utilizzato un’immagine particolare per descrivere l’attesa di una serata così importante: "Direi che sono come un bambino che va a Disneyland per la prima volta. Provo molta eccitazione, orgoglio, emozione e tanta voglia di fare bene e godermi lo spettacolo", ha spiegato l’allenatore del Lens.

Per Digard la sfida contro il Lipsia rappresenta anche un banco di prova importante dal punto di vista sportivo. Il Lens è reduce da una serie di tre sconfitte consecutive nella massima competizione europea e soprattutto dall'umiliazione contro il Como. C'è bisogno di un successo per tenere vive le speranze e riscattarsi.

#2052. Key QPR man set to miss Norwich City trip as 26-year-old nears return

QPR defeated Millwall on Saturday, winning 1-0 through a first-half goal from the returning Nicolas Madsen. However, one man who sat out was captain Jimmy Dunne, who picked up an ankle injury while away with the Republic of Ireland over the international break.

The Hoops make the quick turnaround to face Norwich City on Tuesday, and manager Julien Stephan has admitted skipper Dunne is unlikely to return for the Carrow Road trip. As quoted by West London Sport, he said: “Not definitely, but probably not. It’s not a bad one. I don’t know exactly when he will be able to come back. He is still in a little bit of pain, so let’s see in the next days how the situation evolves.”

In better news for QPR, full-back Tariq Lamptey has returned to training and is likely to be available despite also missing the Millwall win. The 26-year-old has been out with an ankle issue and last played in the 1-1 draw away at West Ham on October 9th.

Stephan has not been afraid to make changes and he is expected to shuffle the ranks for the trip to Norwich City on Tuesday night. Despite Dunne’s absence, he does still have room to make a change at centre-back if he wishes.

Ronnie Edwards captained QPR in the Millwall triumph, and he was partnered by Jake Clarke-Salter at centre-back on their way to a welcome clean sheet. The former Chelsea prospect will be the favourite to partner the stand-in skipper as a result.

But, if he wishes to make a switch, Stephan will have Liam Morrison to call upon. The 23-year-old is yet to make a competitive appearance this season and has been an unused substitute for 10 of the last 11 Championship matches.

If one of the centre-backs was to drop out, it would likely be Clarke-Salter in order to manage his minutes. The 29-year-old has had injury problems over recent seasons but he has only missed two league matchday squads this term.

QPR don’t have the biggest senior squad in the Championship with 26 first-team players. However, they are well stocked in all areas and have already dealt with injuries this term, mainly in attack.

Stephan has shown a willingness to dip into the academy when needed as well. Leon Scarlett has emerged in the senior group, and 20-year-old midfielder Isak Alemayehu has appeared in matchday squads fairly regularly as well.

The Hoops have built the squad well over the past 18 months or so. The summer window saw them boost revamp their options at full-back and in goal, and there’s a balanced and well-rounded squad at Stephan’s disposal as a result.

It means he has room to make changes and ample cover when injuries hit.

#2049. Tardelli omaggia Boniperti: "Vedeva il suo calcio. Oggi non potrebbe essere presidente"

Marco Tardelli, ex centrocampista della Juventus, ha parlato nel corso del documentario dedicato a Giampiero Boniperti, realizzato da Sky Sport e che andrà in onda sui loro canali. Il racconto dell'ex calciatore inizia con un aneddoto: "Gli parlai quando fui acquistato dal Como. Andai nel suo ufficio e capii subito. Dopo dieci minuti di complimenti e raccomandazioni, mi disse: 'Quella collanina e il braccialetto toglili, poi tagliati i capelli'. Mi mise un po' in difficoltà".

Tardelli prosegue raccontando il personaggio: "Amava le squadre serie. Oggi non potrebbe essere presidente: odiava i tatuaggi, non amava i capelli lunghi, a parte i miei. Vedeva il suo calcio. Il rapporto non era facile. Pretendeva di avere ragione sempre e poche volte te la dava, solo in ufficio. Aveva una scala: i più anziani, i più giovani. Cercavamo tutti di tenerci più alti. Qualcosa ci diede. Un anno aveva la foto del Perugia, con cui avevamo perso il campionato. A Villar Perosa mise di fianco la foto del Perugia, dicendo: 'Non chiedetemi niente'".

Infine descrive il suo carattere: "Non era avaro, ma era capace di fare le trattative. Quando andavi dall'altra parte, c'erano i premi: la sconfitta erano schiaffi. A parlare dei premi era molto generoso. A volte arrivava anche a triplicare quelli normali. Avevamo uno spogliatoio fantastico: i muti come Zoff e Scirea, il simpatico Marocchino, il bello Cabrini, Gentile che ci insegnava a dare le botte agli altri. L'Avvocato non si era mai intromesso sui soldi. Si divertiva a dirci: 'Fatelo soffrire quando fa il contratto', ma era difficile".

#2048. Sinner shock, operazione al ginocchio: rientra in primavera

Il tennista sarà operato a Turku il 24 novembre; le prime stime indicano un recupero di circa tre-quattro mesi.

Jannik Sinner ha deciso di sottoporsi a un intervento al ginocchio destro. L’operazione è programmata per martedì 24 novembre a Turku, in Finlandia, e sarà eseguita dal professor Lasse Lempainen. La scelta arriva dopo diversi consulti medici e oltre quattro mesi di terapie conservative che non hanno dato i risultati sperati.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Le prime stime indicano un recupero di circa tre-quattro mesi. Il rientro potrebbe avvenire in primavera, ma i tempi dipenderanno dall’esito dell’intervento e dalla successiva riabilitazione.

Il 12 luglio Sinner aveva conquistato il suo secondo Wimbledon consecutivo battendo Alexander Zverev in finale. Quella partita è stata anche la sua ultima apparizione ufficiale della stagione. Nelle settimane successive il tennista italiano ha cominciato ad avvertire dolore al ginocchio destro.

Il problema è stato identificato come una sindrome della bandelletta ileotibiale, che provoca dolore nella parte esterna dell’articolazione. Per un atleta sottoposto a sollecitazioni continue può diventare particolarmente fastidiosa.

All’inizio Sinner e il suo gruppo di lavoro avevano scelto di evitare la chirurgia. Il percorso prevedeva riposo, fisioterapia e trattamenti specifici, con l’obiettivo di recuperare gradualmente la piena funzionalità del ginocchio senza correre rischi inutili o compromettere ulteriormente la carriera del tennista.

Nonostante i tentativi e i consulti con diversi specialisti, il dolore non è scomparso definitivamente. Il numero due del mondo ha quindi preso in considerazione l’intervento. Decisivo è stato l’ultimo confronto con Lempainen, chirurgo ortopedico finlandese specializzato nel trattamento delle lesioni muscolari e tendinee degli sportivi professionisti.

Tra gli atleti già seguiti dal medico figurano anche i calciatori Ousmane Dembélé e Leonardo Spinazzola. Dopo la valutazione della situazione clinica di Sinner, la scelta è ricaduta sull’operazione a Turku.

#2047. Blackpool set sights on League Two boss as potential Ian Evatt replacement

Blackpool sacked Ian Evatt last week, leaving the Tangerines on the lookout for a new boss. They were defeated in their first game under Steve Thompson’s interim lead, losing to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic 2-1 at home.

Now, a new name has been linked with the vacancy at Bloomfield Road. According to reporter Pete O’Rourke, one man under consideration for the job at Blackpool is Fleetwood Town boss Matt Lawlor.

Lawlor has drawn high praise for his work with the Seasiders’ North West coast neighbours, where he has been in permanent charge since March. The 38-year-old is under contract with Fleetwood until the summer of 2028 at present, so a compensation fee would be required to bring him in as Evatt’s replacement.

Born in Poulton-le-Fylde, Lawlor is a North West native. He played for Blackpool’s youth academy as a youngster before going on to play non-league football with Farsley Celtic, AFC Fylde and Bamber Bridge.

He coached alongside his playing career from a young age, working with Manchester United before joining the Fleetwood Town setup in 2019. Lawlor held various roles in their academy and spent a few spells at their sister club Waterford FC, serving as assistant manager once and caretaker boss twice.

An impressive stint as temporary boss of the Cod Army in January 2026 saw Lawlor given his maiden full-time gig in senior football, and he has made a good impression. He isn’t blessed with resources at Highbury Stadium, but he’s delivered respectable results through fine match preparation and some smart in-game coaching, as shown by the shock Carabao Cup win over Premier League champions Arsenal.

Lawlor’s future at Fleetwood is secure with a contract until 2028, but that might not be enough to fend off interest from elsewhere.

Lawlor’s good work at Fleetwood Town means interest from Blackpool is more than justified. It could prove a tempting opportunity too.

Geographically, he could make the step up to League One without having to move away from home. His past as a youth player at Bloomfield Road could mean there are sentimental temptations as well.

That said, it does feel as though Lawlor is in a good place right now. After various roles in the Fishermen’s setup and at Waterford, he has developed well. He’s still only 38 and in the formative years of his time as a first-team boss too, so may be wary of making the step up too early.

Time will tell whether the rumoured interest comes to anything, with Blackpool sure to be considering plenty of contenders.

#2046. Serie C, doppio cambio in panchina: Auteri lascia il Foggia, Gaburro esonerato dal Desenzano

La 15ª giornata di Serie C porta con sé due cambi in panchina. Il Foggia e il Desenzano hanno infatti ufficializzato rispettivamente la risoluzione consensuale con Gaetano Auteri e l'esonero di Marco Gaburro, decisioni maturate in un momento delicato per entrambe le squadre.

Gaetano Auteri non è più l'allenatore del Foggia. Il club rossonero ha raggiunto un accordo con il tecnico per la risoluzione consensuale del contratto, con la decisione maturata nell'ottica di favorire una svolta per la squadra. Nel frattempo, gli allenamenti saranno affidati temporaneamente a Simone Calori, in attesa della scelta del nuovo allenatore.

"Il Calcio Foggia 1920 comunica di aver risolto consensualmente il contratto con l’allenatore Gaetano Auteri.

L’accordo è stato raggiunto in un clima di piena collaborazione con il tecnico, che ha scelto di compiere questo passo con l’intento di favorire una svolta per il bene del Foggia.

La Società desidera ringraziare sentitamente il mister per la professionalità, l’impegno e la dedizione dimostrati durante tutto il periodo trascorso alla guida dei rossoneri, augurandogli le migliori fortune personali e professionali.

Gli allenamenti, che riprenderanno nel pomeriggio, saranno temporaneamente diretti da mister Simone Calori, in attesa delle decisioni in merito alla nuova guida tecnica della prima squadra".

Si chiude anche l'esperienza di Marco Gaburro sulla panchina del Desenzano. La pesante sconfitta per 1-6 contro l'AlbinoLeffe, unita al momento di difficoltà attraversato dalla squadra, ha spinto la società a interrompere il rapporto con il tecnico, sollevato dall'incarico di allenatore della Prima Squadra.

Gaburro lascia dopo aver contribuito alla storica promozione in Serie C, traguardo che il club ha voluto ricordare e sottolineare nel comunicato ufficiale.

"Il Desenzano F.C. comunica di aver sollevato Marco Gaburro dall’incarico di allenatore della Prima Squadra.

La Società desidera esprimere a mister Gaburro un sincero ringraziamento per il lavoro svolto e la dedizione dimostrate durante il suo percorso alla guida della squadra. A lui va il riconoscimento per essere stato tra i protagonisti della storica promozione in Serie C, contribuendo al raggiungimento di un traguardo unico per la Società e per tutta la città di Desenzano.

Il Club ringrazia mister Gaburro per il percorso condiviso e gli rivolge i migliori auguri per il prosieguo della propria carriera professionale".

#2045. Swansea City, Burnley show interest in 12-goal star ahead of potential January swoop

Swansea City and Burnley are in contrasting positions in the Championship table, with the Swans still inside the play-offs and the Clarets stuck in the relegation zone. While both look to rediscover form on the pitch though, work is going on to identify potential targets for the January transfer window.

Now, a report from Football League World has claimed that the Championship pair are both interested in Huddersfield Town hotshot Joe Taylor. It is said that they are ‘weighing up’ moves for the 24-year-old striker as the next window approaches.

Taylor has been in excellent form this season with 12 goals and three assists in 18 games across all competitions. He is currently under contract until the summer of 2029; that and his form means it will take a handsome fee to prise him away from the Terriers this winter.

Despite his age and the fact he has moved around clubs a fair amount, Taylor is an established name in the EFL with 143 appearances to his bame across the Championship, League One and League Two.

Peterborough United signed him from non-league side Kings Lynn Town, and Luton Town bought him from there. Taylor impressed in loans with Colchester United (27 games, 12 goals, two assists) and Lincoln City (19 games, 10 goals, three assists) but failed to score in 19 outings for the Hatters.

Strong loan form prompted Huddersfield Town to snap him up, and Taylor’s Terriers career has come to life after another successful temporary move, this time to Wigan Athletic (22 games, 11 goals). The Welshman has proven to be a prolific scorer in League One and he is starring at the level once again, scoring for fun in Martin Drury’s attack alongside fellow star Derensili Sanches Fernandes.

Given his success in League One, it feels inevitable that Taylor gets another shot in the Championship. Swansea City and Burnley could offer him such a chance, but they will have to pay a good fee for his services.

Of the two interested clubs, Swansea City are no doubt the more attractive option at the moment. Despite the fact they are currently managerless, the Swans are in the hunt for a Championship play-off finish, and with the help of Jamestown Analytics, they are capable of making some long-awaited strides forward.

But, for Taylor, a move to Burnley may be better. Swansea have all of Zan Vipotnik, Adam Idah and Ross Stewart on the books for their one-striker system, so they do not need another.

As for the Clarets, they have plenty of strikers, but none are impressing. He would quickly jump up the pecking order and into contention for a starting spot against Jamie Vardy, Andreas Hountondji and Zeki Amdouni, and on current form, he’d be backed to beat them.

Alternatively though, a stay at Huddersfield Town could be best. The Terriers will have little interest in selling someone key to their promotion push, and he could end up in the Championship in their colours sooner rather than later.

#2044. Wrexham team news and predicted XI to face Bristol City with Phil Parkinson backed to field an unchanged side

A professional 1-0 victory at Lincoln City extended Wrexham’s unbeaten run to three games, having drawn with Wolves and secured a statement win over table-topping Middlesbrough.

Inconsistency has plagued the Red Dragons’ campaign so far though, struggling to rekindle the fine form which saw them go within touching distance of the Championship play-off places last season. But, Phil Parkinson’s side now appear to have found their feet.

After bringing an end to their five-game winless away run with a victory at Lincoln City, Wrexham are slowly but surely climbing the table and sit in 14th ahead of a trip to face a troubled Bristol City side.

The Robins have lost three on the bounce with pressure mounting on under-fire boss Michael Skubala after another underwhelming showing against Middlesbrough, although the Bristol City hierarchy have publicly backed him to turn them around.

Injuries have played a significant role in Wrexham’s slow start to the campaign, with influential forwards Josh Windass and Nathan Broadhead among those sidelined. Both are expected to return to action next month.

Question marks surround whether Oliver Rathbone will feature at Ashton Gate after being withdrawn on Saturday with a dead leg. Thankfully, Parkinson confirmed after the game that it isn’t a serious issue.

Callum O’Hare hasn’t featured since the defeat to Blackburn Rovers last month and remains a doubt with an ankle problem, while Sam Smith is a long-term absentee with an ACL injury.

In better news, New Zealand international Liberato Cacace, who is yet to make an appearance this term due to recurring calf injuries, is back in training.

Sebastian Revan is also nearing a return having been sidelined with a serious hamstring injury suffered on loan at Burton Albion in February. The 23-year-old is expected to be fit in the New Year.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Whiteman, Dobson, Thomason; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore

The Wrexham side has remained largely unchanged since their much-needed victory over Middlesbrough, with Parkinson seemingly settled on his preferred starting team.

Anthony Patterson will be in goal after two clean sheets from his last three games. Max Cleworth has impressed recently with the experienced Joe Worrall alongside him and both will keep their places alongside standout performer Callum Doyle.

The Red Dragons’ positive form has coincided with Issa Kabore finding his stride in a right-wing back position, which saw him register an assist against Wolves. George Thomason has been equally important on the opposite flank and netted the winner at Lincoln, so both start again.

The midfield pivot of Ben Whiteman and George Dobson remains too, despite Ben Sheaf pushing for a place. Lewis O’Brien and Oliver Rathbone will be keen to impress once again in more advanced positions with Wrexham’s wealth of attacking talent waiting to return from injury.

They were sweating on the fitness of Kieffer Moore ahead of the trip to Sincil Bank, but he played the full 90 minutes at Sincil Bank and will likely lead the line.

#2043. David Storch sends message to 'unreal' Sheffield Wednesday fans

David Storch had to make a big decision at Sheffield Wednesday recently by replacing Henrik Pedersen with Dave Challinor, which is paying off as he has sent an update to the "unreal" Owls fans.

The goodwill towards David Storch and Arise Capital remains in place but they had to make the brave choice to sack Henrik Pedersen, with Dave Challinor coming in and winning his first two league games in charge.

Sheffield Wednesday are firmly in the automatic promotion hunt, let alone the play-off picture, following a 2-1 win away to South Yorkshire rivals Barnsley at Oakwell on Friday night. With other teams in the top half dropping points, they are well-placed to kick on.

Speaking after the Barnsley game on Saturday, Storch took to X (formerly Twitter) to outline his thoughts. He said: "love all things Wednesday! @swfc Fans last night were unreal… we have the best supporters anywhere.

"3 points away away away!! The energy, passion, devotion… You could feel it all the way to Chicago. Love you guys! Missing the live action so much. Hope to see you guys soon!

"And thanks so much for all the well wishes. Getting a little stronger everyday! #WAWAW"

Storch is currently recovering from back surgery, but he will be delighted that his first huge footballing decision has paid off already, with Storch reuniting Simon Wilson with Challinor in the process.

It could prove to be a masterstroke for Sheffield Wednesday, given the pair's previous working relationship and the manager's exceptional record in the EFL. Challinor has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to build winning teams, secure promotions, and get the best out of his players, making him an outstanding appointment for a club with Wednesday's stature and resources.

The pair enjoyed considerable success at Stockport County, taking them from the National League to League One, winning the National League title in 2021/22 and the League Two title in 2023/24. Challinor also boasts seven promotions across his managerial career, having previously enjoyed success with AFC Fylde and Hartlepool United.

His Stockport side narrowly missed out on the Championship in consecutive League One play-off campaigns, losing to Bolton at Wembley in 2025/26 after finishing third. Wednesday should now have the ingredients to challenge for automatic promotion — and anything less than a serious push would be disappointing.

Many of the Sheffield Wednesday fans responded on social media to his update, with one replying: "Delighted to hear you're recovering well after your surgery. You made a great decision bringing in Challinor. A proper football man that'll help build us a club with identity. Look after yourself ☺️"

Another Sheffield Wednesday supporter added: "I have no nails left watching that last night! 😂 Fans were amazing could hear them so much on the TV. Can't wait to see them play at Hillsborough on Saturday! Get well soon Mr Storch. Positive vibes for you and the owls 🦉 💙 🤍"

A further reply from a Sheffield Wednesday fan praised another aspect which has improved at Hillsborough, with one Owl stating: "Fab night at Hirsty’s social last night at the watchalong . Brilliant idea from the club"

#2042. Is Mauricio Pochettino’s job at Manchester United the toughest in the Premier League?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the new manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

“Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one big problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United.  Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

#2041. Exclusive: Swansea City & Burnley in race to sign Huddersfield Town star Joe Taylor

The January transfer window is just over a month away from opening, with EFL clubs already scouting new potential players ahead of the month-long chance to bolster their squads.

For clubs that have players that are starring in their leagues, they're going to face a fight to keep hold of them when it's all said and done, and then there are clubs at various points in the standings of any division that are going to look to strengthen their options.

And for high-flying Huddersfield Town in League One, they have a number of players who may be of interest to teams higher up in the footballing pyramid than they currently are - one player is certainly being looked at by Championship clubs.

Football League World has been exclusively informed that Terriers hot-shot Joe Taylor is a wanted man in the second tier ahead of the mid-season window.

Despite Dutch winger Derensili Sanches Fernandes taking most of the praise and plaudits for the West Yorkshire outfit since his summer arrival from Excelsior, Taylor has been quietly going about his business as part of their dangerous attacking unit, having forced his way back into contention at the Accu Stadium following his loan out to Wigan Athletic in 2025-26.

A look at the amount of pubs within a two-mile radius of every Championship ground this season.

The 24-year-old was shipped out temporarily by previous manager Lee Grant to the Latics, where he found his spark again, scoring 11 goals in half a season for them before returning to Town in the summer under new head coach Martin Drury.

Alongside the aforementioned Sanches Fernandes in a supporting attacking role, where the pair play behind more of a focal point such as Ashley Fletcher or Bojan Radulovic more often than not, Taylor has found the back of the net 10 times in League One already in just 14 outings, proving to be one of League One's best once again.

And that goalscoring performance is not going unnoticed, with FLW exclusively being able to reveal that managerless Swansea City, as well as struggling Burnley are both weighing up a move for the Welsh centre-forward in January.

Taylor has only sparringly played at Championship level before for Luton Town before getting his move to Huddersfield, but there are clubs looking at trying to get the attacker a move up the pyramid.

Swansea of course lost head coach Vitor Matos to Strasbourg last week, but it will not stop them eyeing up targets ahead of January, and Taylor is on their radar, even with a strike-force of Adam Idah, Ross Stewart and Zan Vipotnik to choose from - the latter was the Championship's top scorer last season but has failed to fire in 2026-27, and theoretically could be cashed in on to open up the space for another new forward.

Burnley meanwhile are in the Championship relegation zone and haven't won in Fabio Celestini's four matches in charge - they have centre-forward options like Jamie Vardy, Zeki Amdouni and Andreas Hountondji, but with a lack of goals coming from that particular trio, Taylor is being considered as a January option.

Whether Huddersfield would cash in on Taylor mid-season with their promotion aspirations remains to be seen, but given he's under contract until 2029, it'll likely take a significant amount of cash to prise him away from Drury's squad.

#2040. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#2039. Manchester United consider legal action over JJ Gabriel departure

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United are prepared to consider legal action if evidence emerges that another club approached academy forward JJ Gabriel without permission.

The 16-year-old announced his departure from Old Trafford in a social media video on Tuesday and is expected to join Real Madrid in January. According to The Times and ESPN, United remain concerned about the circumstances surrounding his proposed move, although no breach of transfer regulations has been established.

Gabriel has been absent from United since September, when he requested the cancellation of his registration. The teenager remains registered with the club, and United could explore legal or regulatory options if evidence of an unauthorised approach emerges.

The Independent reports that United do not want to punish Gabriel for actions they believe may have been taken by adults involved in his future. Real Madrid have been widely linked with the forward, but his transfer has not been formally completed.

Gabriel joined United’s academy in 2020 and was named the club’s young player of the year last season. He featured for the senior side during pre-season but has not made a competitive first-team appearance.

The youngster is eligible for a move within the European Union under an exception to FIFA’s rules on international transfers involving players aged under 18. In his farewell message, Gabriel thanked United for helping him develop during his six years at the club.

His expected move to Madrid would bring that association to an end, although questions remain over the process leading to his departure. United have not announced legal proceedings, and there has been no finding of wrongdoing by Real Madrid or any other club.

#2038. Charlie Austin tells Alex Neil to 'shut up' after Millwall v QPR comments

Former Queens Park Rangers goalscoring icon, Charlie Austin, has hit out at Millwall boss, Alex Neil, following the Scot's criticism towards Hoops winger, Paul Smyth, following Saturday's heated all-London affair at The Den.

Rangers continued their recently impressive form with a third victory in five matches by defeating the Lions 1-0 in SE16, courtesy of Nicolas Madsen's strike in the first minute of first-half stoppage time.

However, it is fair to say that the remainder of the contest wasn't without controversy, as the hosts were reduced to 10 men just 15 minutes into the contest after Zak Sturge's late challenge on the Northern Ireland international winger.

Although the statistics certainly showcased that Julien Stephan's side could have won the game by more if they finished their 31 attempts at Lukas Jensen's goal, much of Neil's post-match press conference centered around Smyth's involvement throughout.

The Saturday lunchtime victory saw Rangers end the Championship's 16th matchweek in seventh on 27 points, whilst Millwall sit 16th with nine fewer points.

Smyth, 29, is capable of featuring on either flank, and certainly caused plenty of issues for the Lions defence on Saturday in his 74-minute cameo, although Neil certainly had differing opinions.

“I spoke to Smyth about diving on the pitch in general. We had five players booked, and most of them came from him falling over," he said.

“The sending off – if he’s not offside, he’s not offside. If it’s a sending off, it’s a sending off. I’ve always been really straightforward with that sort of stuff. If it’s found that he’s guilty and he deserves to be sent off, I’m not going to argue that.

Neil was also booked for a verbal altercation with the Rs man, adding: “I told him to stop diving.

“I think what it was, it’s an element of frustration, but I’ve watched Paul Smyth for years. He’ll probably come up here and tell you he never dives, but I’d beg to differ.”

Austin is a former teammate of Smyth's at Loftus Road, having returned to W12 back in 2020, scoring 15 goals in 59 appearances during his second spell, which lasted for two seasons.

The 37-year-old now offers regular opinions on Championship developments, and he defended the 26-time international when asked on his YouTube channel to give a verdict on Sturge's dismissal.

"I'm going to say yes," he said. "Paul Smyth does well there. He gets his body in the way and knows what's coming.

"Alex Neil comes out and says he was diving all around the pitch. Shut up mate.

"You'd like to have Paul Smyth in your team," Austin stated.

"Seriously. The threat he gives when 'we' have the ball, but when 'we' haven't, he presses and uses his pace well. He entices defenders to get close to him, which brings a foul and he anticipates the touch is coming.

"But, for Alex Neil to come out and say that, I thought it was a stupid and naive comment."

The ex-Swindon Town frontman has offered his services after Ian Holloway was dismissed as manager

Austin knows exactly what it takes to achieve promotion to the Premier League, having done exactly that with the Hoops and West Bromwich Albion.

The former striker was certainly encouraged by Rangers' performance against their London rivals this weekend, especially the way in which they continued to impose themselves on the contest despite the hosts' desire to remain defensively solid.

Rangers and Millwall fans, do you agree with Alex Neil or Charlie Austin? Comment below!

Neil's comments, unsurprisingly, split opinion depending on which side of the fence those who watched the 90 minutes sat on, but that doesn't take away from the threat Smyth can possess, with the attacker already scoring and assisting three goals this campaign.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

He Smyth does cause issues for defenders with his pace both with and without the ball.

Unfortunately I thought the sending off just spoiled the game. Millwall defending deep and no threat. The first 15 mins QPR were lively and attacked with 6-7 players coming forward.

Arconte should have done better with his opportunity were he snatched at the ball.

As for Alex Neil maybe he should have kept quiet but it was the heat of the moment.

As for Charlie Austin who I rated as a player even back in his Swindon days should also act professional and let the officials deal with it.

However, the officials were very poor in my opinion lots of wrong decisions and linesmen who dies not keep up with the last defender.

Manchester United have been linked with Como midfielder Nico Paz, although Real Madrid’s buy-back option and the absence of reported negotiations leave considerable uncertainty over a potential move.

#2035. Chris Wilder snaps at reporter in Sheffield United press-conference after Sydie Peck question

With three wins in their last four matches, Sheffield United have found some form heading in to the busy December period.

And one of Chris Wilder's stars of the campaign has been Sydie Peck, who remained at Bramall Lane despite transfer attention from elsewhere, is operating on another level.

Peck went through the entire 2024-25 Championship season without scoring, but after notching five goals last season, he's already matched that tally from midfield in 16 outings in 2026-27 - adding three assists to that tally too.

Peck - who joined United from Arsenal's youth setup in 2021 - rarely plays together with fellow midfield youngster Oliver Arblaster, who came through the Blades academy, but they started alongside each other in the engine room in the 4-0 rout of Watford this past weekend.

That pairing has been a source of contention for many United supporters in recent times - Peck's run in the first-team on a regular basis only really began when Arblaster was sidelined with a knee injury two seasons ago, and the latter was left sidelined more often than not when he was fit and ready to return last year.

They worked pretty well together against an abject Hornets side, but Wilder seemed to object to a question posed to him about whether or not they can work as a good pairing on a regular basis.

Wilder seemed utterly bemused, noting they've only played together six times in midfield, winning three and losing two, and he believes that fans are waiting for Peck and Arblaster to 'fail' as a partnership for whatever reason - you can watch the full rant below.

Arblaster's emergence in Sheffield United's relegated Premier League team in 2024, following a stint on loan at Port Vale, was a genuinely exciting moment - despite the drop back to the Championship, United had a player that was ready to start week in, week out in the Championship.

Sadly, his knee injury set him back a year, but it allowed Peck to emerge from the shadows and become the player he has now developed into - whilst still a raw talent, there's a reason why Premier League clubs have been circling in recent times from the likes of Newcastle United and Sunderland.

If Peck continues to seriously impress, then Sheffield United will have a big decision to make in the January window should bids arrive at their door - selling Andre Brooks, Callum O'Hare and Gus Hamer for decent money in the summer though could mean the club are in a stronger financial position than many think.

Every player has a price though, and with January fast approaching, there's a chance that the Peck and Arblaster partnership may not have that much time to flourish.

#2034. Who stays and who leaves Manchester United under Mauricio Pochettino, Gary Neville reveals list

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches. He has a massive job ahead of him, with many pundits and former players terming his situation the toughest in the Premier League.

Gary Neville believes the Argentine will need several transfer windows to get the squad where he wants it, if he gets that much of time at Manchester United.

The former captain shared his views on which players he expects Pochettino to keep, and who could be heading for the exit.

Neville believes Senne Lammens should remain part of the plans, although he expects Pochettino to bring in another goalkeeper to give him some competition for his place. At the back, he backed Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro to stay, while suggesting Ayden Heaven needs a loan move to the Championship.

“Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville said on Stick to Football.

In midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

Mason Mount, however, is not part of his plans. Neville said: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

Neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

“Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”

He expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

Neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term plans.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

“But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”

Pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting CP in January 2020.

Bruno Fernandes has scored 113 goals in 341 appearances for Manchester United and has regularly carried the creative responsibility in midfield for the Red Devils.

His performances have remained amazing despite United struggling in recent times. Despite a sluggish start to the last season, Bruno Fernandes went on to register 21 Premier League assists, breaking the league’s single-season record.

Mauricio Pochettino will now have the opportunity to speak directly with the midfielder and make his own case for him to remain part of the project.

However, there are several issues still to resolve. The financial terms, length of the proposed contract and release clause will all need to be discussed before an agreement can be reached with the Portuguese midfielder.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to hold talks with Bruno Fernandes over his Manchester United future, with the club captain yet to agree a new contract at Old Trafford.

According to Fabrizio Romano, the new United head coach will now become involved in discussions with the Portuguese midfielder, whose current deal expires at the end of the season. The club have the option to extend it by a further 12 months, but are also keen to secure a longer-term agreement.

Manchester United have already held negotiations with Fernandes, but the 32-year-old has rejected two contract offers. Romano explained that Pochettino’s involvement could be an important part of the talks, although the final decision will rest with Bruno Fernandes and United.

Fernandes’ future is not settled at Manchester United and with Pochettino arriving at the club, he may have a different thought about his contract situation. Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

#2030. 5 players should follow Ernie Weaver out of Sheffield Wednesday in January

Sheffield Wednesday find themselves in a peculiar position regarding their academy, as a lot of young homegrown talents introduced themselves to the fanbase at Championship level last season due to "circumstances," but now need to find regular game time elsewhere.

That's the view of new Owls boss Dave Challinor, who has hinted that a few loan departures may be on the cards for some of the younger players in the squad who put themselves in the limelight during their difficult campaign last season under administration.

Wednesday's ability to build a squad over the past summer window has meant that, despite some fans looking forward to seeing these young players become the core of a new-look side, they've fallen by the wayside.

Challinor stated that Ernie Weaver, one of the early standouts from last season before being sidelined for the majority of the campaign with a foot injury, could be someone who leaves on a short-term deal in January, following the likes of Charlie McNeill, Cole McGhee and Reece Johnson, who all played some part in the Championship last season.

These five players should also be tipped for a loan move in the near future to get some valuable game time, too.

Dave Challinor namedropped a couple of other players who could leave the club on loan at some point in the near future. One of those was fellow centre-back Gabriel Otegbayo.

The Irish Under-21 international epitomised the chances that young players got last season while the club was in administration. The former Burnley academy man made 35 Championship appearances last season, including a run of 23 starts in the final 25 games.

Otegbayo began this season as one of the first-choice defenders under Henrik Pedersen, too, starting four of the first five in league action and scoring in his one appearance off the bench against Bromley in that 7-2 demolition.

Since that fifth game, though, the 21-year-old hasn't started in the league, and he's to feature in a matchday squad in League One under Challinor. Indeed, his only appearance under the new boss came in the 4-0 EFL Trophy defeat against Accrington Stanley.

Wednesday fans weren't too enamoured with his performances in the early stages of the season, and also feel that he could benefit from a spell elsewhere.

The other player mentioned by Challinor as a potential loan option was midfielder Jarvis Thornton, who signed a new two-year deal with the Owls this past summer.

The 20-year-old has been at Wednesday since he was eight years old and was one of the many academy graduates who made their first-team debuts last season. He was one of the main features of their run to the EFL Cup third round, and he made 23 league appearances, too.

This season, though, Thornton has been one of the main victims of the midfield being strengthened at Hillsborough. The returns of Barry Bannan and Jaiden Heskey, plus the addition of Billy Mitchell, have made it difficult for him to get minutes.

His last league appearance came in that 7-2 win over Bromley nearly three months ago, and he's made a matchday squad just once since then.

The new contract ensures that the decision-makers at Wednesday think he has a bright future, but he may need to begin to realise that elsewhere.

It was a proud moment for Sean Fusire against Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy, as he wore the captain's armband for the first time. Unfortunately, the Zimbabwe international hasn't been able to stake a claim for regular league minutes this season, though.

The 21-year-old, unlike the others on this list so far, has actually spent time out on loan from Sheffield Wednesday. He spent the second half of the 2024/25 campaign at Carlisle United in League Two, but was then thrust into Championship action last year.

Which fanbases can improve on their current atmosphere offerings? The computer has had its say....

Only seven players played more league minutes than Fusire last season, but the full-back only has a couple in League One this year, coming on for the final stages of Henrik Pedersen's final game in charge at Doncaster Rovers.

Under Challinor, he has appearances in cup competitions, but hasn't made a league squad yet. You feel that, once the January window opens, he'll be one of the first out the door.

It was a pleasant surprise for Wednesday fans to see George Brown starting against Accrington Stanley. It was the 20-year-old's first appearance in nearly 11 months after a season plagued by injury.

Like Weaver, it was a real frustration to see him sidelined during the campaign in which he'd have gotten exposure at Championship level. He scored twice in just seven second-tier games last year, including one of their two wins all year at Portsmouth, and looked very promising.

He needs game time, but he won't get it at Hillsborough anytime soon. A good loan move away, perhaps at the top of the National League, could be massively beneficial to his chances of making it back in the senior fold in South Yorkshire.

There arguably isn't a more exciting talent on Sheffield Wednesday's books right now than Will Grainger. The Welsh Under-19 international only just turned 18 earlier this month, and broke through towards the end of last season, scoring in a 4-1 defeat against Oxford United.

He also extended his contract with the Owls over the summer, but he, too, has been a victim of the strengthening of the squad, especially across the frontline.

Do you think Will Grainger will be a major player in Sheffield Wednesday's bid to rise back up the EFL? Let us know in the comments.

Wednesday won't just be wanting to loan him out to any club for minutes; they'll be taking great care with this decision, as the 18-year-old could be a cornerstone of this new era under the Arise ownership.

A good League Two move could work wonders for Grainger and put him in brilliant standing to properly break into the Owls' senior side next season, if they remain in League One.

#2029. How can Mauricio Pochettino help Manchester United players to perform again?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to rediscover their winning mentality after agreeing to become the club’s new head coach.

Manchester United announced Pochettino’s appointment just over 24 hours after confirming the departure of Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager is believed to have agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford.

He takes charge of United who sit in an embarrassing 18th place in the Premier League table. They have managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, coming against Ipswich Town.

There is little time for the new head coach to settle in, with a difficult first fixture against fierce rivals, Liverpool already awaiting him.

Speaking to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino made it clear that restoring confidence in the team and improving performances will be his immediate priorities.

“The most important thing for now is to start to work hard to recover that feeling about being a winner – to win games, to perform.”

The Argentine hinted at sticking with the current crop of players to help them rediscover their form.

“We need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for them to perform.”

Pochettino’s first match in charge will be one of the toughest possible introductions to English football’s biggest rivalry. Manchester United travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, giving Pochettino very little time to work with his squad before his first outing.

The new head coach faces a mountain ahead of him. He has walked into one of the most difficult jobs in world football. United have struggled so far into the season and they need results quickly to get them out of the relegation spots.

Pochettino has spoken about bringing back the winning feeling at Old Trafford, but his first challenge will be getting a response from his players who have managed only one league win in 10 games so far. That is far from Manchester United standards and Pochettino will be hoping he can instill some confidence back in the team.

The Liverpool game will offer an early indication of how his players respond to the change at United. A positive result would provide immediate relief for the under pressure United but the longer-term job of rebuilding United will take much more than one match.

Ecuador’s late World Cup surge has given Chelsea a useful development signal through Moises Caicedo and Kendry Paez before Xabi Alonso’s first pre-season friendly on 28 July.

Chelsea confirmed that Caicedo and Paez reached the Round of 32 after Ecuador’s dramatic 2-1 win over Germany.

For Alonso, the contrast between the two Chelsea midfielders matters as much as the result.

Caicedo captained Ecuador through the pressure game, with We Ain’t Got No History highlighting the Chelsea midfielder’s leadership role in a win that rescued their tournament.

Paez, meanwhile, sits in a different phase of his rise.

Read Chelsea has already looked at how Alonso must handle Paez’s development curve, and this knockout place sharpens that argument.

Alonso inherits a midfield loaded with senior names, transfer noise and immediate pressure.

Caicedo gives Chelsea the proven pillar. Paez gives them the controlled upside.

Ecuador’s run now gives Chelsea both at once.

For Chelsea, that is the ideal succession picture: leadership today, patience for tomorrow.
