#2005. Arsenal Women vs London City Lionesses preview: Gunners face tough test at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal look to build on their recent win over Liverpool as they return to the Emirates Stadium but will face an impressive London City Lionesses side who are a potent attacking threat on their travels.

Renée Slegers’ team have struggled to convert their strong performances into points in the league this season. They have lost their last four WSL games at home, however, becoming the first team in WSL history to draw four successive games at home.

Their bad run must come to an end. They have taken just three points from their first nine league games so far this season, scoring a miserable total of 10 goals. However, they look like they have more in the tank and will need to be much more clinical in front of the goal.

The day also marks Slegers’ 50th game in charge of the WSL. The Dutch manager has only lost six league games so far this season, with only Chelsea having a better record from teams that have been ever-present in the division.

Arsenal can’t take their opposition lightly after London City’s impressive recent form. They have won two and drawn once in their last three away league games, scoring 12 goals.

Eder Maestre’s side has become a potent attacking force. Daniëlle van de Donk has provided four assists this season, and Delphine Cascarino has scored three goals and provided two assists.

Kadidiatou Diani can be dangerous. She has scored or assisted in all four of her league games away from home this season.

London City’s attacking prowess means they are a far different proposition to some teams Arsenal have faced at home. They have been in a positive situation for 62.7 per cent of their league minutes this season, the highest in the WSL.

Arsenal will have to deal with the attacking threats but look to utilise their ball possession better. Giving London City an opportunity to counter could make an already tough afternoon even tougher.

Alessia Russo comes into the game having found the net in her last three WSL games and will be key in converting Arsenal’s chances into goals.

The Gunners also showed their fighting spirit in their midweek clash against Barcelona. They drew 1-1 at Camp Nou to become the first side to take points off the Spanish giants in the Women’s Champions League at home since April 2024.

Slegers’ team will feel emboldened by that result but will have to change their tactics against London City.

They have won all seven games against Arsenal so far, scoring an impressive 22 goals and only conceding once. However, given London City’s recent away form, they will be hotly favoured.

They certainly have the quality to take all three points, but they must finally convert their dominance into a comfortable home win.

#2004. Jamie Gittens suffers Chelsea injury blow with England U21s

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Gittens has withdrawn from the England Under-21 squad. He suffered an ankle injury during Tuesday’s qualifier against Kazakhstan at Molineux. The Chelsea winger left the ground on crutches. He has returned to Stamford Bridge, where the Jamie Gittens injury will now be assessed by the club’s medical staff.

Gittens picked up the knock after a challenge during the second half of England’s win over Kazakhstan. He was withdrawn as a precaution. He did not take any further part in the match. England have been careful not to overstate the issue and no further reports have come out further.

The 21-year-old struggled to put weight on the affected ankle and was seen limping around Molineux after full time. That prompted an immediate release back to his club, rather than any attempt to assess him further in camp.

England Under-21 boss Lee Carsley addressed the injury directly after the game. He confirmed the nature of the knock and the decision to send Gittens home.

“Jamie got a kick on his ankle,” Carsley said after the match. “We never take any risks. With the age of these players, we don’t ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back.”

England’s statement on the squad changes, detailed in a report from Football.London, confirmed the wider fallout from the fixture.

“Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

Gittens has been an unused substitute in every Premier League fixture Chelsea have played this season, with his only two appearances under Xabi Alonso coming in the Carabao Cup. Those minutes have offered him little platform after his big summer move.

Alonso’s squad selection has been a talking point since he took charge. Our earlier look at Xabi Alonso’s squad choices at Stamford Bridge covered how competitive things have become. An ankle injury will not change his pecking order in the short term. It does, though, remove any chance of him pushing his case this week.

Chelsea’s break has brought other headlines too. Cole Palmer also withdrew, for entirely different reasons, after his recall by senior boss Thomas Tuchel to the full England squad. Chelsea will be watching both returns closely before domestic football resumes.

Chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

Given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Fans can follow how the squad shapes up before the next fixtures through our recent line-up updates. Further news on Gittens is expected once Chelsea’s medical staff finish their evaluation.

#2003. Arsenal transfer interest in Alphadjo Cisse: Arsenal face a £50m decision as AC Milan youngster attracts Premier League interest

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal transfer interest in Alphadjo Cisse is starting to take shape. Arsenal are monitoring the development of AC Milan starlet Alphadjo Cissé, although his sensational start to the season could prove to be costly for Mikel Arteta.

The 20-year-old has made a blistering start to his Serie A career and attracted interest from a number of Premier League clubs after his impressive displays so far. Arsenal are reported to be interested.

The Gunners are among several clubs, including Brighton, keeping tabs on the player, according to Italian football news website Tuttomercatoweb. The striker is rumoured to be worth up to 60 million euros. That’s an eye-watering sum for a player who is just starting out in his professional career.

Cissé was signed by Milan from Hellas Verona in February 2026 but was allowed to finish the season on loan at Catanzaro.

Prior to joining the San Siro, he had already showcased his potential with six goals in 22 games in Serie B. He has made a huge impact since moving up to the top division.

Cissé has found the net five times in nine Serie A games this season. He has also chipped in with three goals in four Europa League games, making a total of eight goals in 13 games.

This has made him an important addition to the Milan squad. He is also versatile, as he can play as an attacking midfielder or higher up the park.

Arsenal may find his versatility attractive. Arteta likes players who can play in different positions and with injuries, and with a busy fixture list, he will want to have players who can do that.

The main issue could be that Milan are keen to keep their young star.

It is reported that the Italian club have turned down a verbal offer from Brighton and are looking to extend Cissé’s contract, which currently runs until June 2030.

This indicates that Milan is considering his future, rather than looking to make a profit. It also demonstrates just how quickly his reputation has developed.

Arsenal have the funds to target exciting young talent, but would they want to spend so much on Cissé?

There is no indication that he would be an instant replacement for Arsenal’s current attacking options. However, Cissé’s age, goal-scoring ability and versatility make him an interesting prospect.

This could be one to keep an eye on beyond January. Milan have little motivation to sell, and Arsenal might want to see how he develops before committing themselves.

Cissé has already hit the ground running in Italy and now needs to prove that his initial success can turn into something more consistent.

#2002. Bruno Fernandes breaks silence on Man Utd contract offer

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s most creative player since his arrival to the club in 2020.

The 32-year-old is approaching the final months of his current deal, which expires at the end of the season. United do have the option to extend his contract by another 12 months, keeping him at Old Trafford until 2028.

While they can extend his contract for a year, Manchester United are actively pursuing a deal to tie Bruno Fernandes beyond 2028.

Bruno Fernandes himself has now confirmed that the club have offered him a new contract, but the midfielder has made it clear that he does not want discussions about his future to become a priority right now.

Fernandes confirmed that an offer had been made but dismissed suggestions that he was holding out for a better salary or a longer agreement.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

He also insisted that money has never been the reason behind his decision to remain at United, despite having opportunities to move elsewhere in previous transfer windows.

“If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here,” Fernandes said.

The Portugal international added that he could have earned considerably more by accepting offers from other clubs, but always chose to continue his career in Manchester.

Fernandes revealed that discussions initially took place towards the end of last season and continued when the players returned for pre-season.

However, the United captain believes the current situation at the club makes it the wrong time to focus on his personal future.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side,” he explained.

“I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting in 2020. He has scored 75 Premier League goals for the club and set a new competition record for assists in a single season last term.

Bruno’s comments don’t sound like he is holding United hostage demanding more pay or refusing to sign a new one. The intention as told by Bruno Fernandes just show his leadership trait about putting the team first. He has no immediate intention of making his contract situation the centre of attention. That will be a sign of encouragement for the fans as well.

Manchester United need to start winning games again. When they do and surely Bruno Fernandes will be at the centre of it, the contract talks can resume and take priority.

#2001. Manu Koné: Roma slap £86m price tag on Chelsea target

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

“There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I said it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of important players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

For now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

#2000. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

#1999. Manchester United players face tougher training demands under Pochettino, report claims

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United players have reportedly been told to expect a further increase in training demands under Mauricio Pochettino after Sunday’s Premier League match against Liverpool.

The new manager arrived at Carrington on Wednesday following his departure from the United States national team and has had less than four days to prepare for his first match in charge. According to The Sun’s report, published on Saturday evening, United’s players have already noticed longer and more intense training sessions compared with those under former manager Michael Carrick.

The newspaper reports that Pochettino has initially concentrated on introducing his tactical approach, with more demanding physical work expected once the Liverpool fixture is over. An unnamed source claimed the players had already felt a significant change in tempo and workload, despite the Argentine having only a limited period to work with the squad.

Pochettino is also reported to have taken a hands-on approach during training, regularly stopping drills to explain his instructions directly to players. The report adds that the 54-year-old has been communicating in English with United’s staff and has asked his predominantly Spanish-speaking coaching team to do likewise.

Pochettino’s first assignment is Sunday’s visit to Anfield, with United looking to improve on a difficult opening to the Premier League season. The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager conducted an extended training session on Saturday as preparations for the fixture continued.

However, the reported emphasis on fitness and conditioning suggests that his wider changes at Carrington may become more apparent after the Liverpool match. United have not publicly confirmed the details of the training programme described in the report.

#1998. Martin Ødegaard sends clear message to Arsenal amid Bayern Munich transfer rumours

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Ødegaard has spoken out about the speculation surrounding his future. He has stated he would like to stay at Arsenal for the future.

The captain has also admitted that talks about a new deal have not yet begun. Ødegaard is currently under contract until the summer of 2028. This leaves Arsenal with an important decision to make over the coming months.

Bayern Munich are being linked with an interest in the midfielder according to reports from Germany. The Bundesliga giants are said to be keeping their eyes on the player’s situation.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, Ødegaard was quick to dismiss the speculation. He made it clear he is settled in north London and sees his future being at the Emirates Stadium.

There is no suggestion that the 27-year-old is seeking a move. Although comments do highlight a contract issue that Arsenal will be keen to resolve in the short term.

The Norwegian’s laid-back attitude should be encouraging for supporters.

He has made it clear that he is happy at the club and wants to stay here for the time being. This means that there is no need to panic.

However, Arsenal will have to get him to sign on the dotted line. Leaving his captain in the last year of his contract with no progress would cause an unnecessary distraction.

Since his permanent move from Real Madrid in 2021, Ødegaard has become a key player in Mikel Arteta’s plans. He has grown into a team leader and is one of the most influential players in the dressing room.

His importance has been shown by his inclusion in all 10 of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far this season. He has scored three goals.

This is a big improvement on last season, where he was hampered by injuries and failed to make much of an impact in front of goal.

It wouldn’t be a shock to see Bayern Munich show interest in Ødegaard, but don’t take this as a sign he is close to a move.

There is little reason for Arsenal to consider losing their captain. He brings so much more to the team than just his technical ability and has been relied upon by Arteta to lead by example.

The midfielder was also pivotal in the 1-0 win over Hull City on 7 November, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute to give the league leaders three crucial points.

Arsenal have put themselves in a good position in the title race. Keeping their key players happy will be important in the second half of the campaign.

The Gunners will be focused on their game against Newcastle United on 21st November.

Arsenal fans have no real reason to panic at the moment, with the captain wanting to stay at the club and his comments suggesting he is happy.

However, it would be a good idea for the club to try and ensure his long-term future at the club. Ødegaard is still an important part of Arteta’s strategy, and ensuring he stays at the club would be a smart move.

I can’t wait to walk out there on Saturday.

Plea for unity or simply the new man confirming his passion for this club – we knew that anyway. It ramps up, rather than damping down expectations which is fine: Parker gives himself a lot to live upto. No hiding place then, go on and ‘make us proud!’

#1996. Joao Pedro Injury: Chelsea Forward Misses Brentford Defeat

Graeme Hanna is the site lead of Read Rangers and also writes about West Ham for Read West Ham. A Rangers season-ticket holder and freelance writer, he has previously written for Vital Rangers, Rangers Review, Football Ground Guide and Give Me Sport, and has a long association with the Follow Follow fanzine.

Joao Pedro missed Chelsea’s 3-0 Premier League defeat to Brentford with a knee problem, and the injury has since ruled him out of Brazil’s squad for the friendlies against Australia and India.

He was absent from Xabi Alonso’s confirmed lineups against Brentford, with Chelsea turning to other forward options instead.

Brazil’s coaching staff confirmed the withdrawal, pointing to the same knee issue that kept him out of the derby. Chelsea have not set a firm return date for Joao Pedro, leaving supporters to wait for further updates during the international break.

The Joao Pedro injury situation took a new turn when the Standard reported that he is seeing a specialist during the international break to speed up his recovery.

According to the Standard, the forward is using this pause in the calendar to get ahead of the problem rather than wait for Chelsea to resume domestic action.

Chelsea have not issued their own statement on the specialist visit, and the club’s official line on Joao Pedro’s fitness remains limited to his withdrawal from matchday duty.

Full detail on the reported treatment can be found in football.london’s reported injury update, which first carried the specialist claim alongside Xabi Alonso’s comments on the striker’s season.

Until Chelsea confirm otherwise, the Standard’s report stands as the clearest picture of how the club are handling the knee concern.

It suggests a measured approach, with recovery prioritised over rushing Joao Pedro back into contention for the next fixture.

Before the injury forced him out, Xabi Alonso had made his admiration for Joao Pedro clear. The Chelsea manager ranked the forward among the Premier League’s elite strikers, alongside Manchester City’s Erling Haaland.

“If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there, Haaland for sure is there.

“So I would rate him that way. He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, and to be a nominee for not just this month but more months. I am not surprised, but really happy with the kind of player that we have here with João.”

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Alonso must lean again on the depth built into his squad.

His approach to rotation, part of the squad management this season, faces another test while his in-form forward is unavailable.

#1995. Liverpool v Manchester United: Five classic wins at Anfield

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

#1993. Arsenal Women held by London City Lionesses despite Frida Maanum goal

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

The Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

#1992. Pep Guardiola Speaks Out as Man City Found Guilty of 114 Charges

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 financial charges, the Premier League has confirmed. The verdict follows an eight-week hearing that opened almost two years ago. It closes one of the most significant disciplinary cases in the competition’s history.

Former head coach Pep Guardiola has already broken his silence. Reaction to the Pep Guardiola Man City charges verdict is spreading fast across the division, with Chelsea among the clubs watching closely.

Guardiola joined Manchester City in 2016 and turned them into the dominant force in English football. He left his post earlier this summer, with the club having already worked through plans to replace Pep Guardiola at City.

His exit means he holds no formal role at the Etihad. Yet he moved quickly to make his loyalty clear once the ruling landed. According to the football.london report that first carried his statement, Guardiola posted directly to his supporters.

“I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman [Khaldoon Al Mubarak], Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has confirmed that the club intends to appeal the verdict. The statement from Guardiola comes to City’s defence despite him leaving the role this summer. He is still viewed as the man who built this era of success, even though he no longer sits in the dugout at the Etihad.

The Pep Guardiola Man City charges case matters just as much to Chelsea as it does to Manchester City themselves. Chelsea, along with Arsenal and Tottenham, are among the Premier League clubs directly affected by the outcome. Every point City may have gained through breaches has a knock on effect further down the table.

Most top flight clubs including Chelsea are now pushing for City to face relegation as a consequence of the verdict. Some are reported to be weighing up legal action of their own. Guardiola has spoken about Chelsea before, including Guardiola’s previous comments on Chelsea. This latest statement fits a pattern of public backing for Manchester City, despite the criticism now directed at the club.

For Chelsea supporters, the case is not just about points on a table. It touches on the integrity of seasons they competed in directly. That is why so many rivals are refusing to let the matter rest with a guilty verdict alone.

Manchester City’s appeal process is now the next stage in a case that has already run for nearly two years. Ferran Soriano has made clear the club will contest the findings. No date has been confirmed for when that appeal will be heard.

Until then, no points deductions, penalties or changes to past titles have been confirmed by the Premier League. Chelsea and their rivals will be watching the appeal timeline just as closely as they watched the original hearing. The final outcome could still be a long way off.

#1991. Manchester United’s 34-goal defensive record shows scale of Pochettino’s task

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the new head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

According to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

The Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

The defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical plan was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the issues exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

For Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

#1990. Declan Rice’s latest Arsenal evolution shows why Arteta wanted him tied down

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Declan Rice’s new contract shows how much of an asset he is to Mikel Arteta. His recent performances show why.

The England international has reportedly signed a new five-year deal which will keep him at the Emirates Stadium until 2031. The contract is a reward for the midfielder who has been instrumental in Arsenal’s success since he moved to the club in 2023 from West Ham.

Rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta quickly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

His physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a new attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

The reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

#1989. Alex Scott Chelsea Transfer Blocked as Bournemouth Eye January Stay

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bournemouth will block any Alex Scott Chelsea transfer in January. That is according to reports from the Daily Mail and BBC Sport. Both outlets say the Cherries want to keep their young midfielder as they fight to protect their Premier League status this season.

Chelsea have been linked with serious interest in the 22-year-old. Reports suggest the Blues have already tested Bournemouth’s resolve with a bid worth close to £64 million. Bournemouth have given no indication they are willing to negotiate. Scott, the reports say, simply is not for sale this winter.

Reports in the Daily Mail and on BBC Sport state that Bournemouth have no intention of sanctioning a sale this winter. The club’s hierarchy reportedly view Scott as central to their survival plan, wary of leaning on new signings mid-season rather than trusting the squad they already have.

A fee of around £64 million, first reported by Football London, is said to have been offered by Chelsea during recent discussions.

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023. He has quickly become one of the most sought-after young midfielders in English football. Interest from a club the size of Chelsea shows how far his reputation has grown, though Bournemouth’s stance makes a January move increasingly unlikely.

Scott’s rise has been underlined by his first appearance for England. He came off the bench for a 20-minute cameo as Thomas Tuchel’s side beat Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League. The manager praised him afterwards.

“Alex Scott has maybe one of the best performances in midfield in the Premier League since the start with Bournemouth.”

“Individually he’s one of the outstanding midfielders so he clearly deserves to be with us.”

“He took another step into the right direction. Very impressive and happy that he is on that route. Now he plays in Europe for Bournemouth and deserves to be with us.”

That praise from their former manager will only increase Chelsea’s interest. Scott’s energy and composure suit the identity Xabi Alonso wants to build at Stamford Bridge. The Spaniard has already shown he is willing to rotate his squad, as seen in Xabi Alonso’s squad management decisions this season.

Chelsea travel to face Bournemouth in the Premier League soon. It is a fixture that will give Alonso a close look at a player repeatedly linked with his club. Build-up to that game is already underway, with team news arriving ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

The prospects of an Alex Scott Chelsea transfer happening in January now look slim. Supporters hoping for fresh competition in central midfield may need patience, with Chelsea more likely to revisit their interest when the summer window opens.

#1988. West Ham United v Preston North End | Scott Parker delivers shock line up

Preston North End at home – and a traditional 3pm kick off on a Saturday afternoon is Scott Parker’s home debut as West Ham United manager. The expectation is high after many fine words from fan favourites Parker and his assistant Mark Noble – and of course the two week break from football has only heightened the anticipation as bottom club Preston come to visit.

After beginning with a draw and a loss within his first three days at the helm, Parker gets to show us ‘his’ West Ham line up and set up this afternoon. Having had a two week break to work with the bulk of his West Ham side, we’ll get to see a Scott Parker XI now along with the manner in which he plans to set his team up.

The first line up of the Scott Parker era has been announced: And there’s a couple of big shocks with third choice keeper Fin Herrick selected in place of Mads Hermansen AND Edson Alvarez getting a recall!

Herrick | Veltman, Mavropanos, Morato, Mayers | Engels Alvarez Mukasa | Bowen, Piroe, Austbo

Unsurprisingly we’re all in the upbeat and full of hope camp: – especially after seeing that line up.

The game is not televised so why not join the Hammers chat watch along on YouTube? Audio coverage is on BBC Radio London and we’ll be backwash player ratings as soon as the final whistle is blown.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

This was a Nuno game with Nuno tactics. When will Parker instill his own ideas on our play? I’ve seen nothing different so far with Parker, in fact I think Nuno would’ve worked it out in the second half better than Parker — that difference probably being a Kante introduction for Ausbø who was ineffective

This should be a fairly comfortable win, I’m thinking 3-1, I’ll be in arms if it’s anything less than a win…

How refreshing is that! If they click, we could be in for a good day. I hope young Herrick has a good game, and Alvarez shows the fans what they have been missing. Mayers will hopefully cement his place in the team with another confident display. This could be the day things start to turn.

Is the line up really a shock or is it what most of us would have picked ourselves?

Alvarez in. At last a manager with balls backed by Noble Gets My full backing

Very surprised at the line up there appears to be 11 players in their correct positions I cannot remember the last time that happened

#1987. Roy Keane questions Manchester United standards after Liverpool humiliation

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has criticised the players’ performance and questioned supporters applauding them after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, insisting the early red card was no excuse for the manner of the loss.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge unravelled when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes at Anfield. Liverpool scored twice inside 13 minutes and added two more goals after the break, leaving United 19th in the Premier League.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Keane challenged the suggestion that United’s performance was understandable because they had played most of the match with 10 men.

“Fans are applauding. Applauding what?” he asked, before describing the performance as “rubbish”.

Keane argued that United should have shown greater fight and quality, claiming Liverpool could have scored eight or nine goals. He also questioned why responsibility for the club’s problems so often fell on managers, owners and executives rather than the players themselves.

Some travelling supporters applauded the team after the final whistle, potentially recognising the difficulty of playing more than 80 minutes with a numerical disadvantage. Keane, however, viewed the reaction as evidence of declining expectations.

Keane also challenged fellow former United captain Gary Neville, who had suggested the early dismissal made the result more understandable. Neville was far from satisfied with United’s performance, though, and separately accused the club’s hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen the defence.

The disagreement reflected two concerns surrounding United: the players’ response to adversity and the quality of the squad available to Pochettino. Liverpool’s goals came from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the hosts creating numerous further opportunities.

Pochettino defended his players’ commitment afterwards and questioned Yoro’s dismissal, arguing that Alexander Isak had not established control of the ball when the defender challenged him. United have taken just eight points from 11 Premier League matches, leaving their new manager with little time to improve results. They travel to Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action.

Keane’s criticism adds to the scrutiny surrounding the squad following another heavy defeat to their fiercest rivals. For Pochettino, the immediate challenge is to improve defensive organisation while restoring confidence in a side struggling near the bottom of the table.

#1986. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1985. Chelsea’s Reggie Watson gets next chance under Alonso

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Reggie Watson Chelsea news continues to build, according to football.london, with the 16-year-old further establishing himself as one of Xabi Alonso’s wildcard options in the first-team squad. Watson has been named in both of Chelsea’s senior squads for their Carabao Cup ties this season.

He was an unused substitute in the second-round win over Luton Town, then made his full Chelsea debut in the 6-3 win over Leeds United at Stamford Bridge. Watson played the first 45 minutes against Leeds, a reward for his progress since Alonso took charge at Chelsea over the summer.

Every stage of Watson’s rise has come through football.london’s reporting, with Chelsea yet to make any official comment on his long-term role in the squad. The outlet’s football.london report traces how the teenager has moved from pre-season fixtures into genuine first-team contention this term.

Watson played a big part in Chelsea’s pre-season tour, completing the full 90 minutes of the opening match against Western Sydney Wanderers. He was also part of Chelsea’s travelling squad for the Brentford defeat before the international break. Watson was left out of the matchday squad list for that game, though, as explained in our Brentford line-up report.

Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli was the Chelsea youngster named on the bench for that Brentford trip and came on late in the match, football.london added.

Watson’s form has caught attention away from the first-team picture too. He was one of three Chelsea youngsters nominated for Premier League 2’s Player of the Month award for September, alongside Chizaram Ezenwata and Leo Black, according to football.london.

Black recently signed a two-year contract at Chelsea after impressing on trial, while Watson built his own case by scoring three goals in September. That form explains why the Reggie Watson Chelsea story keeps developing. Alonso keeps pulling him into senior squads instead of leaving him with the academy alone. The head coach has shown similar willingness to adapt his squad elsewhere, as detailed in Alonso’s recent rotation plans.

Chelsea are reported to be facing Portsmouth in a behind-closed-doors friendly this weekend, according to football.london, though the club has not confirmed the fixture publicly. Alonso reportedly wants to keep his squad sharp during an extended three-week international break.

Chelsea’s academy side, known as Cobham Next Gen, have no fixture of their own this weekend. That gap could leave Watson free to train or travel with the first-team squad again, football.london reports.

The teenager will try to impress Chelsea’s first-team staff in that friendly. Nothing is confirmed yet about what his involvement will be once the senior squad returns to action after the international break.

#1984. West Ham 1 – 1 Preston North End | Player ratings as Parker drops more points

West Ham again conceded in the first half and spent the rest of the game peppering Preston’s goal – four efforts hit the woodwork but to no avail until Mavropanos’ second half equaliser. A lack of clinical finishing cost Scott Parker’s side dear as the points were shared.

Encouraging early touches with his feet and a willingness to catch rather than punch initially inspired confidence. Failed to get his fists to a corner, the ball striking Piroe on the head and looping over Herrick to give Preston a simple goal to create their lead. A superb double save just before half-time kept West Ham in touch after Mayers’ poor header. Grew in stature in the second half, notably catching balls where Hermansen might have punched.

Good early interplay with Bowen down the right. Unlucky not to score when his effort crashed against the post immediately after Bowen had hit the woodwork. Replaced by Souček on 78 minutes.

Solid enough first half without really being tested. Slipped in to meet a deflected Engels cross and equalise in true Mavropanos style.

Looked far more comfortable in the combative centre-back role, without being seriously tested for pace. Met Solomon’s second half cross with a header that was blocked.

Solid enough first half until a dreadful defensive header gifted the ball back to Preston, with Herrick rescuing him through a superb double save. Booked after misjudging his control and pulling down an opponent. Replaced by Scarles on 78 minutes.

A great through ball released Piroe for West Ham’s first decent opportunity. Excellent work out wide, crossing with his weaker foot to allow Mavropanos to equalise. Lots of wide running in a much more advanced position than under Nuno. Looked better for it.

Making his first appearance of the season, showed little sign of rustiness. Should have equalised after a well-worked corner, curling into the side-netting. Looked increasingly at home sitting in front of the defence and moving remarkably quickly across the turf. Quick feet in the opposition box led to a shot poked agonisingly close, but just wide. A pretty good shift on his return; surprising he lasted until 90 minutes, when Magassa replaced him.

Should have taken a first-time shot with his right foot, but instead shifted onto his favoured left and scuffed the chance in the first half. Needs to produce more. Evidently Parker agrees as he was replaced by Castellanos on 57 minutes.

Struck the post with a right-footed effort as West Ham pressed for an equaliser. Had the beating of his full-back in the second half, making frequent runs down the right and crossing with his weaker foot. Several shots but lacked that killer punch – as did the whole attack.

Should have opened the scoring after ten minutes when sent through one-on-one by Engels, but the goalkeeper saved. Lots of trying and ‘nearlies’ but too little output. Booked on 82 minutes for a professional foul. Not enough from the striker.

A decent early effort from 25 yards went straight at the goalkeeper. Immediately after the restart, stepped inside and struck the bar with a brilliant curling right-footed shot. Replaced by Solomon on 57 minutes at which point West Ham’s pace and zip largely vanished. There’s a lesson in there…

On for Austbø, 57 minutes. One jinking run inside produced a cross met by Morato’s head, but the effort was blocked. Looked very right-footed and unable to beat defenders on the outside. West Ham were poorer for the substitution of Austbø and Solomon’s introduction.

On for Mukasa, 57 minutes. Fluffed his lines on 85 minutes, looping a back-post header over the bar.

On for Mayers, 78 minutes. One decent cross late on. Understandably rusty-looking.

On for Veltman, 78 minutes. Almost won it in the 94th minute with a back-post header tipped over by Preston’s goalkeeper.

I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. He is a lightweight, easily pushed off the ball. Hardly a single pass to a colleague, except the usual backwards. When he does make a run, he if very quick, but it usually end in a dead end.

Scores and general comments too low on all the players. Poor result but some good performances excl. Mukasa and Tatty. The style was chalk and cheese and it will come

Yes I do wonder what has happened to Pablo and Kante. Whilst he seems lacking in technique we always seem to do better with Pablo in the team. He gets stuck in and causes disruption for opponents in a way no one else does. Kante runs hard the the rest and seems capable of making things happen. Play Bowen as a number 10 so he create all over the field.

The players are gripped with anxiety and a collapse of confidence. Relegation plays a huge part in that, a lack of character too.

When things were going well after a slow start the team seemed to exude confidence, and there was talk of us romping the league and walking back to the heady heights of the Premier League.

We hit a slippery patch, however, and the boys have not dealt with it at all. The confidence has drained from us. Dominating possession means nothing. It’s a false statistic to concentrate on. We can’t create clear chances and outscore the opposition. Going behind and chasing points is another matter. Seems to happen virtually every game.

Solutions? Well that’s down to Parker and Noble. It speaks volumes of the void we find ourselves in that Noble would risk his status as a legend at the club to become involved in this debacle. It also shows his commitment to the club.

Ultimately, Parker needs to find a way to win games and get some confidence back into the boys. Otherwise, we will struggle to make the play-offs.
